execution.observation: The test asserts that a stale structured amount derived from a prior retained conversion-rate value is accepted after that rate is replaced, while the active frame was compiled through compile_boundary_recall with its direct action/tool roles hard-bound.

reason: Section 43 of the pre-existing v0.6.3 specification defines the hard Recall Obligation as including action/tool grounding dependencies, not only direct schema fields. The conversion rate materially grounds the emitted amount, so a conforming consequence boundary must carry it as a hard grounding dependency. E0-v2 therefore demonstrates that the runtime cannot independently prove a host-supplied boundary is complete; it does not demonstrate that rc4 semantics permit omission of the rate.
positive_result: The trace exposes a practical enforcement surface: low-level/faulty hosts can violate the existing consequence-bound obligation and still receive a valid use fence because current rc4 does not machine-check semantic completeness of host-supplied action/tool grounding roles.
non_claims: The successful pytest step does not prove external prevalence.
The trace does not close W5.
The trace does not prove universal dependency completeness or incompleteness.
The trace does not authorize merging the existing v0.7 SRSC feature branch as a new semantic contract.
next_action: Reclassify the existing G3 structured consequence-origin prototype as opt-in enforcement of the existing action/tool grounding contract, preserve MemoryUseFence as the sole use-time owner, and evaluate it with conformance-specific negative controls before any semantic-version claim.
